standard_prerequisites.name: The first two entries of the diagonal
standard_prerequisites.statement: The fundamental group of the circle is the integers, and the second homotopy group of the two-sphere is the integers.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two base cases of the induction.

standard_prerequisites.name: Stability for spheres
standard_prerequisites.statement: For k at most 2n-2 the group in degree k+1 of the (n+1)-sphere equals the group in degree k of the n-sphere.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the inductive step, applied with k equal to n.

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy groups and truncations
standard_prerequisites.statement: The n-th homotopy group of a pointed type is the 0-truncation of its n-fold loop space.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the definition through which the two sides of the inductive step are compared.

core_obligations: Establish the two base cases of the induction: the first homotopy group of the circle and the second homotopy group of the two-sphere are the integers (source lines 1860-1861).
For n at least two, check the numerical hypothesis n at most 2n-2 that makes the stability theorem applicable (source line 1862).
Apply stability for spheres with k equal to n to identify the group in degree n+1 of the (n+1)-sphere with the group in degree n of the n-sphere (source lines 1862-1863).
Combine that identification with the inductive hypothesis to obtain the claim for n+1 (source lines 1863-1864).

proof_roadmap.step: Base cases: the circle and the two-sphere entries of the diagonal.
Inductive step: apply stability with k equal to n and use the inductive hypothesis.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 1855-1857: the n-th homotopy group of the n-sphere is the integers. The proof (source lines 1859-1865) is an induction on n whose step is not visible in the statement: the two entries of the diagonal that the author has already computed are the base cases, and for n at least two the numerical hypothesis n at most 2n-2 makes the stability theorem applicable, which identifies the group in degree n+1 of the (n+1)-sphere with the group in degree n of the n-sphere and closes the step with the inductive hypothesis. Short as it is, the proof carries the whole reduction from the general statement to the two computed entries, and both the range check that licenses stability and the induction are written out in the retained text.
